## Overview

Revenue grew in every region this quarter. Hyphenation and justified text make longer paragraphs look even, especially in internationalisation-heavy documents such as this one, where words get long.
See @tbl-rev and the [methodology note](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/typst.html) for details.

The growth came from three sources: new customers in the east, higher renewal rates in the north, and a smaller number of discounts across the whole portfolio.
The west grew the least, mostly because two large contracts moved to the next quarter.

## Results

### By region

| Region | Revenue | Change |
|--------|--------:|-------:|
| North  | 1,240   | +12%   |
| South  | 980     | +8%    |
| East   | 1,105   | +15%   |
| West   | 760     | +3%    |

: Revenue by region, in thousands. {#tbl-rev}

### By quarter

Each region reports its revenue at the end of the quarter.
The totals below add the four regions and compare them with the same quarter a year earlier.

| Quarter | Revenue | Change |
|---------|--------:|-------:|
| Q1      | 3,610   | +6%    |
| Q2      | 3,840   | +7%    |
| Q3      | 4,020   | +9%    |
| Q4      | 4,085   | +10%   |

: Revenue by quarter, in thousands. {#tbl-quarter}

The trend is steady, and the last two quarters grew faster than the first two.
We expect the same pattern next year, provided the large contracts in the west close on time.

## Method

The summary uses a short pipeline:

```r
sales |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2026) |>
  dplyr::summarise(total = sum(revenue)) -> totals
x <- totals$total != 0
```

The figures come from the finance ledger and are checked against the invoices each month.
Regions with fewer than ten invoices are merged with their neighbour before the change is computed.

### Checks

A second block shows how the change is computed from two totals.

```r
change <- function(now, before) {
  (now - before) / before
}
change(4085, 3714) >= 0.1
```
